resources.string: Brainrot Stopper needs a few permissions to block apps, read daily usage, and detect short videos. Each step explains what the permission does and what stops working if you deny it. You can finish at any time. The app will tell you what is disabled. Browser URL blocking over a VPN is deferred, so this version does not ask for VPN access.
Android needs this service to see which app is in front and to draw the block screen. There is no other supported way to block one app without root. It does not read message content.
Blocking is off. Schedules and rules cannot be enforced until you enable this service.
Lets Brainrot Stopper read how long each app was in front today, so a daily timer can stop an app at its limit. Usage totals stay on the device.
Daily timers are off. Blocking by schedule still works.

Best-effort short-form detection reads the playback duration from a media session. It does not read message content. If an app does not publish a duration, detection stays off and whole-app rules still apply.
Short-form detection is off. Whole-app blocking and daily timers still work.
Android shows the required status notification while the blocking service runs. Without it you cannot see that the engine is active.
The blocking engine still runs, but its status notification is hidden.
Some phones stop background services to save power. Exempting Brainrot Stopper helps the blocking engine stay alive. This is recommended, not required.
Recommended: without the exemption some phones may stop blocking in the background.
Not needed on this Android version
All permissions granted. Blocking, daily timers, and short-form detection are available.
Onboarding can finish now. These features are disabled or reduced:
This device has no Settings screen for that permission. You can grant it later from Android Settings.
